explanation: A son of Jonathan and grandson of King Saul, who was lame in both feet. He was taken into King David's household.
The king of Israel and a central figure in 2 Samuel, known for his piety, skill as a warrior and musician, and as the author of many psalms.
King Saul's eldest son and a close friend of David. Jonathan died in battle together with his father.
Israel's first king and father of Jonathan. He was rejected by God because of his disobedience and replaced by David as king.
A servant of Mephibosheth who was appointed to manage Mephibosheth's estates and assist him after he was taken into David's household.
A town east of the Jordan River where Mephibosheth lived before being brought to David.
God's unconditional love and favor. In this context, it refers to David's kindness and grace toward Mephibosheth, despite his connection to Saul's house.
